## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
One Important defect needs fixing: `requirement_proven([])` now returns `True`, so a requirement with no criteria is reported as proven, where the base code returned `False`. This review traced both functions in `app/proof.py` against the base implementation in the pinned diff and read `tests/test_proof.py`. It did not run the tests. One verified strength: `reviewed_batch` raises a clear `ValueError` on an empty batch, and the added test covers both that path and the mixed true/false outcomes.

## Changes
The PR rewrites `requirement_proven` to compare a sum of `proven` flags against the number of criteria. It also adds a `reviewed_batch` helper that rejects empty batches, plus a module constant `REVIEW_HINT` and a new test module.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/proof.py:2 — correctness — Return False when criteria is empty — With `criteria=[]`, `sum(...)` is `0` and `len(criteria)` is `0`, so `requirement_proven([])` returns `True`. The base version, `bool(criteria) and all(...)`, returned `False` for the same input. The diff drops the emptiness guard, and `test_requirement_with_evidence` never passes an empty list, so nothing catches the change. — Any requirement with no attached criteria is now reported as proven, which overstates proof status; no test protects against this regression. — Fix: Restore the guard, e.g. `return bool(criteria) and all(item["proven"] for item in criteria)`, and add `assert not requirement_proven([])` to `tests/test_proof.py`.
